clue.text: Cracking surrounds that, strangely, could be stunning

indicators.note: the cracking word literally surrounds the shuffled THAT
'strangely' says THAT turns up in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone admires a striking piece, perhaps a cracked vase, and finds it oddly stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like an adjective of praise, which chimes with the definition; it is the verb form, the word that gets split open.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a view that takes your breath away stuns you.

clue.text: Insect going underneath cheese for a moment

indicators.note: in a down clue the insect is placed below the cheese

explanation.surface: A fly lands under the cheese for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the insect first, but in a down entry 'underneath' puts it last.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb of time: doing something for only a short spell.

clue.text: A number under three finally put away

indicators.note: 'finally' takes only the last letter of three

explanation.surface: A sum where a number is filed under three and then put away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put away' is informal for food consumed, so it matches the past participle EATEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to put away food is to consume it, often a lot of it.

clue.text: So touchy, second to go under the judge

indicators.note: S, the usual abbreviation for second, has to leave SORE
in a down clue what is left sits below THE REF

parts.note: a referee, or ref, judges a match
touchy = SORE; remove S for second

explanation.surface: A thin-skinned person bristles at being ranked second, under the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the standard abbreviation for second; SORE without it is ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'So' and 'therefore' both introduce a conclusion.

clue.text: Duck taking drink on lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the drink sits on top of the lake's letter

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A duck takes a drink on the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The duck and lake belong together in the surface, so it is easy to miss that L is just an abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a small freshwater dabbling species with a green wing patch.

clue.text: Relatives terribly regal in play

indicators.note: 'terribly' says REGAL comes out mangled

explanation.surface: Family members behave terribly royally in a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Apt, since the tragedy turns on a king betrayed by his daughters.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of Shakespeare's tragedies.

clue.text: Lowest point where drain needs repairing

indicators.note: a broken drain gets put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: The lowest spot in the yard, where the drain always needs fixing.
explanation.walkthrough: The drain sits at the low point in the surface, which disguises it as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the point of the sky directly below an observer, the opposite of the zenith; now any low point.

clue.text: Dark-haired female animal circling land

indicators.note: the animal goes round the word for land

parts.note: to land a fish is to net it

explanation.surface: A dark-haired woman watches an animal circle a patch of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Land' reads as a noun, but it is the verb: to land a catch is to NET it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French feminine form, from brun (brown), used for a woman with brown or dark hair.

clue.text: Nobility recorded item under leadership of Gladstone

indicators.note: the leader of Gladstone is its first letter

parts.note: an item recorded in a ledger is an entry

explanation.surface: Aristocrats appear in the record under Gladstone's government.
explanation.walkthrough: Gladstone was a Victorian British prime minister, which makes 'leadership' read as his premiership.
explanation.definitionFit: The gentry are the class just below, or loosely including, the nobility.

clue.text: Where ships are, mostly

definitions.meaning: the main is the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old word for the open sea, so ships are literally in the main.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In the main' means mostly, for the most part.

clue.text: Minimum of gaiety in terrible, sad song

indicators.note: the smallest part of gaiety is its first letter

explanation.surface: A terrible, sad song with barely a trace of cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minimum' could suggest a count, but here it is the single leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament sung at a funeral, from the Latin 'dirige' that opened the Office of the Dead.

clue.text: Friend adjusted part of camera

indicators.note: the letters of FRIEND are adjusted into new positions

explanation.surface: A friend fiddles with a camera part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adjusted' fits the camera surface so well it hides its role.
explanation.definitionFit: The finder, or viewfinder, is the part of a camera you look through.

clue.text: Wine to drink in, blow it!

definitions.note: the definition is 'it', something one blows

indicators.note: the wine takes IN in, as a drinker takes in a drink

explanation.surface: A frustrated drinker curses at the wine: blow it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow it!' sounds like an oath; read literally, 'it' is the thing to be blown, a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: 'it' stands for a woodwind instrument, sounded with breath through a reed.

clue.text: Colour likely to run?

definitions.meaning: cowardly, apt to run from danger

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a dye that bleeds in the wash; the second sense is a coward who runs away.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow is a colour, and yellow also means cowardly.

clue.text: Saver, 50% off lion and cougar, say?

indicators.note: cutting half off lion keeps two of its four letters

parts.note: a cougar is an example of a feline

explanation.surface: A bargain-hunter's sale: half price on a lion and a cougar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saver' reads like a shopper, but it is something that saves a life.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeline is a saver, something that rescues someone.

clue.text: Records go in work of art

parts.note: tapes record things; recordings are tapes
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Records being entered into a catalogue of artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' is the noun, as in 'have a go', meaning a try.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a textile picture woven or embroidered on a loom, like the Bayeux example.

clue.text: Seriously premature, where chicks are being nursed

indicators.note: the nest is held inside the word for premature, as a baby is held while nursed

explanation.surface: Seriously premature chicks being nursed back to health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seriously premature' reads as one phrase, but 'Seriously' is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adverbs describe acting with sincere, grave intent.

clue.text: On time, trains transported container?

parts.note: to train someone is to teach them
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A container carried on trains that run to schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like railway carriages, but it is the verb, teaches. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea chest is a wooden box used to ship tea, later for moving house.

clue.text: Moderated part of articles, often edited

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following words

explanation.surface: Articles are toned down because they are so often edited.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word breaks, with the S of articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Softened means moderated, toned down.

clue.text: Home Counties remedy, safe

parts.note: the Home Counties surround London in the South East of England

explanation.surface: A reliable home remedy from the leafy counties around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties around London, in the South East, abbreviated SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives describe being protected from harm or loss.

clue.text: Instructions to trim edges at the front

indicators.note: trimming a word cuts a letter off it
says the trim is made at the start, so the first letter goes

explanation.surface: A gardener's instructions to trim the front edges of the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the front' says which end loses a letter: the B goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: commands given by someone in charge, in the plural like the definition.

clue.text: Medical device empty say, call nurse at last

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its outer letters

parts.note: to call on the phone is to ring

indicators.note: only the last letter of nurse is kept

explanation.surface: A medical device is empty, so call a nurse at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the fodder here, not a signal for an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a plunger-and-needle tool for injecting or drawing off fluid.

clue.text: Priest's possible vow to repair a bicycle

indicators.note: repairing puts the parts of A BICYCLE together another way

explanation.surface: A priest vows to fix a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' makes the definition fair: celibacy is one vow a priest may take.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic priests take a vow of celibacy.

clue.text: Spicy dish eaten by cannibal, Timothy!

indicators.note: the dish is swallowed inside the next words

explanation.surface: A horrified shout: the cannibal Timothy has eaten a spicy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma between the words hides the join.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry, popular in Britain, cooked in a wok-like pan.

clue.text: Male lumberjack

explanation.walkthrough: Feller is informal for fellow, a man; it also means one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberjack fells trees, and a feller is a chap.

clue.text: Source of yarn a shopping centre used up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' reads the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: A knitter uses up yarn bought at a shopping centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of yarn' suggests a storyteller, but it is an animal whose wool is spun.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic-leaning description: a South American camelid whose fleece is spun into wool.

clue.text: Star element

definitions.meaning: the principal performer in a show

explanation.walkthrough: Star and element pull towards astronomy or chemistry; the first sense is the lead role in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the top-billed performer in a production, and the heavy metal with symbol Pb.

clue.text: Material containing nitrogen from a bodily organ

parts.note: material in the sense of real, physical
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Nitrogen-rich matter produced by the body, as urea is by the kidneys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' reads as a noun, but it is the adjective, meaning real.
explanation.definitionFit: Renal means relating to the kidneys, a bodily organ.

clue.text: Problem with vision has arisen, yet to be corrected

indicators.note: the letters are wrong and must be put right

explanation.surface: An eye problem has come up and has not yet been corrected, as with glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrected' fits vision so neatly that it hides its role.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: tired, aching eyes from screens or reading are one such problem.

clue.text: New charity baked something sweet for a special occasion

definitions.text: something sweet for a special occasion

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A new charity bakes a treat for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: The charity bake sale surface fits the answer's world.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the candle-topped treat baked for one particular annual celebration.
